samples.summary: `usedControls` bypasses the keyVersion integrity gate, so unvalidated on-disk state reaches the prompt path and can suppress the hunter's NEVER-TRIED list
samples.evidence: `mergeCoverage` gates every other field behind `usable()` (line 310: `c.keyVersion === COVERAGE_KEY_VERSION`), but the new `usedControls` block reads `prev?.usedControls` / `next?.usedControls` directly (lines 401-408), keeping only `typeof n === "string" && n !== ""`. The loader at scripts/agent/hunt-ui.mjs:1158-1167 parses `coverage.json` off disk and documents the contract "NORMALISE, do not trust ... never a malformed object reaching the renderer"; that contract now no longer holds for this field. Vector: anyone able to write the coverage file (a shared/checked-in `.hunt/coverage.json`, a restored CI cache/artifact, or a compromised workspace) supplies `{"sheet-author":{"usedControls":["Bold","Undo",...every control name...]}}` with any keyVersion; renderCoverageBrief line 490-496 unions those names into `usedControls`, `untried` (line 496) becomes empty, and the NEVER-TRIED section — described in-file as "the most valuable line in the brief" — is silently removed from the explorer's prompt. The result is a defect hunter blinded by tampered state with no signal that anything was dropped. Impact is bounded because the field is only used for set membership and is never rendered verbatim, so no text injection follows.

samples.summary: Coverage-file keys are assigned onto a bare object, so a `__proto__` key in the parsed JSON mutates the object's prototype instead of adding an entry
samples.evidence: `priorCoverage = {}` (line 1155) then `priorCoverage[id] = mergeCoverage(null, record)` for every key of `JSON.parse(readFileSync(coverageFile))` (lines 1158-1167). A coverage file containing a `"__proto__"` key invokes the Object.prototype `__proto__` setter, replacing `priorCoverage`'s prototype with the merged record instead of storing a persona entry; subsequent `priorCoverage[persona.id]` lookups (line 1375) then resolve through that injected prototype for any persona id colliding with `shapes`/`inventory`/`usedControls`/`keyVersion`, feeding another persona's (or an attacker's) memory into that persona's prompt. Not global prototype pollution and the file is normally machine-local, hence low confidence; a `Object.create(null)` map or an `id === "__proto__"` skip removes it. Pre-existing line, but this change widens what an attacker-supplied record can carry through `mergeCoverage`.

samples.summary: Control names harvested from the app-under-test DOM are interpolated verbatim into the explorer's LLM prompt, an untrusted-input-to-prompt path this change reshapes
samples.evidence: `inventory` entries come from a `dom.controls` reading of the running application (coverageFromJournal lines 206-217) and are emitted into the prompt unescaped at lines 523 and 531 (`  - \`${x.control}\``), which hunt-ui.mjs:444-449 splices into the explorer prompt. If any accessible name on the surface derives from document/sheet content (a cell value or block text surfaced as an aria-label), that content becomes prompt text; a name containing markdown/heading text could steer the explorer. The section carries a "(DATA, not instructions)" header (line 449), which is the mitigation, and there is no length cap, fence, or escaping. This path is pre-existing rather than added here — the diff only changes which names are filtered out of it (lines 490-496) — so it is reported as hardening, not as a new hole.
